placeholders.days: whole days since the relevant event — the student's last visit, a past failure, or the length of the current practice streak
placeholders.streak: number of consecutive correct drills in the current run
placeholders.attempts: how many attempts the student previously needed on this problem
placeholders.secret: name of the secret being taught or tested in this stage
placeholders.idiom: the memorisable form of the secret — the line the student is to keep in the hand
placeholders.score: problems answered correctly in the final test
placeholders.requirement: name of the gate dimension that is short: recognition, understanding, implementation, or retention
placeholders.shortfall: how far the short gate dimension sits below its threshold, as a percentage

greeting_first: You are here for search. Sit.
I will ask one question of everything you write. How many operations.
A linear scan is an answer. It is almost never the answer.
You will learn to discard half the world at a time and lose nothing worth keeping.
greeting_returning: You returned. The interval is where you left it.
greeting_after_gap: {days} days. Nothing here narrowed while you were absent.
Away {days} days. We resume one step back. That is the cost, not a punishment.
{days} days. Recall halves faster than skill. I will measure both.
Gone {days} days. I do not scold. I only record. Begin.
lesson_intro: One rule: {secret}. It removes half the work at every step.
{secret}. Attend to the boundary, not the loop.
This is small. It collapses a class of problems. {secret}.
lesson_memorise: {idiom} Keep it in the hand, not in notes.
You will not derive this under a clock. Take it now: {idiom}
{idiom} Repeat it until you no longer read it.
drill_wrong: No. Your invariant broke. State what is true of lo and hi, then answer again.
Wrong. That midpoint overflows. Use lo + (hi - lo) / 2 and retry.
No. That loop does not terminate when the interval is two wide. Trace it by hand.
Wrong boundary. You returned the first true. I asked for the last. Again.
No. The predicate must be monotonic before you may halve. Check that first.
drill_streak: {streak} in a row. The interval closes without you thinking about it. Continue.
{streak} correct. That is fluency, not luck. Do not slow now.
trial_intro: I name nothing now. Read the constraints and decide.
No label. Choose the technique yourself.
You are alone with the problem. The bounds will tell you what to do.
Decide. Then be prepared to defend the decision.
fail_wrong_pattern: Wrong technique. The bounds were 10 to the ninth and the order was given. That was the signal.
No. You searched the array. It was the answer you should have been searching.
That approach cannot pass here at any speed. Back to the constraints. We read them together.
Wrong choice. Ask what is monotonic in this problem, then choose again.
fail_timeout: Time. Your solution works. It is slow. Find the logarithmic solution.
Time. You scanned where you could have halved. That is the whole diagnosis. Again.
Time. Nothing you wrote was incorrect. It was linear. Here that is enough to fail.
Time. The knowledge is present, the speed is not. That is a drill problem, and drills fix it.
fail_wrong_answer: Right technique. Wrong boundary. You are off by one on the high side.
The idea held, the loop did not. Test it on an array of two.
Correct approach, broken edge. Check the case where the answer is the first element.
You chose well and executed badly. That is the cheaper failure. Repair it and return.
Your predicate is not monotonic as written. Fix the predicate, not the search.
success: Accepted. Slow, but accepted. The next interval is narrower.
success_fast: No wasted operations. That is the standard here.
praise_exceptional: That was well done. You searched the answer, not the array.
Correct at both boundaries, and quick. Few manage the boundaries at all.
Your best work in this hall. You did not guess the invariant. You held it.
Nothing wrong, nothing wasted. I have no correction to offer.
praise_major: I have measured many students. Most are fast once, and then absent. You were neither. {score} of {total}, at the first sitting. You have earned my respect.
You arrived solving in n operations and stopping there. You do not stop there now. That change was work, not talent, and work is the only thing I weigh. You have earned my respect.
I do not encourage. I weigh, and I rule. I have weighed you: first attempt, {score} of {total}, nothing wasted. The ruling is that you have earned my respect.
memorisation_detected: You recall answers. You do not hold the invariant. Those are different things. Another problem.
The problems you have seen, you pass. The fresh ones, you fail. That is memory, not search. We go back one step.
You remember where the boundary fell last time. You cannot derive it. So I will move it.
improvement_noticed: You failed this {days} days ago. Today you solved it. Recorded.
You needed {attempts} attempts once. Today, one. That is improvement.
This was linear when you last sat here. It is not now.
What stopped you does not stop you. Note the method, not the relief.
commitment_noticed: {days} days without a gap. Most stop before now. You did not.
You return after every failure. I am counting.
Talent is common. Attendance is not. Continue.
Consistency is the one thing I cannot teach. You brought it yourself.
gate_locked: Not yet. {requirement} is short by {shortfall} percent. Return when it is not.
The gate holds. Recognition is short — you know the halving, you do not yet see when it applies.
No. Understanding is short. You can write the loop. You cannot state its invariant.
Implementation is short. The idea is sound and the boundaries are not. Drill, then return.
Retention is short. Last week's work has already decayed. Review first.
gate_open: The gate is open. Come when you are ready.
You meet the thresholds. The final test waits.
Nothing is short any more. The timing is yours to choose.
Enough. You may sit for it.
final_test_intro: I name no technique here. That was the point of every drill before this.
Three problems. Nothing labelled. The clock runs.
No help from me. Only what you carry.
Read the constraints. They are the only hint you are given.
victory: It is done. You do not scan where you can halve. That was all I had to teach.
Passed. The next master will assume you can do this. He will be right.
Finished. Carry the invariant out with you.
